title: Loan Accounting Note: Interest Accrual and Installment Billing on Equipment & Vehicle Loans
content:
**Rule.** Interest on an Equipment & Vehicle Loans loan is simple interest accruing daily on the principal balance using the actual/365 day-count convention. On each installment due date the interest for the installment period — from the day after the previous due date (the funding date for the first installment) through the due date, both inclusive — is booked as one accrual entry billed with that installment, rounded once to cents, and the next due date moves forward by one installment period (one, three, six or twelve calendar months by the installment frequency; when the day does not exist in the target month the last day of that month is used). The installment due is the loan's installment amount, of which the billed interest is the interest share and the rest the principal share; the final installment is the billed interest plus all principal then outstanding. A deferred installment is not billed on its original date: its period simply runs on to the next due date. While a loan is in nonaccrual status, accrual entries are still booked for the record but no late charge is assessed on them.

## The interest figure

The interest billed with an installment is the sum, over every calendar day of the installment period, of the principal balance outstanding that day, multiplied by the contract rate applied, divided by 100 and divided by 365; that single figure is rounded to cents once.

**Hypothetical worked example.** Principal of 100000.00 outstanding throughout a 30-day installment period at a contract rate of 7.3: the daily principal summed over the period is 3000000.00; multiplied by 7.3, divided by 100 and divided by 365 it gives 600.00 of interest. If the installment amount is 2000.00, the interest share is 600.00 and the principal share 1400.00.

## Installment periods

| Installment frequency | Period |
|---|---|
| monthly | one calendar month |
| quarterly | three calendar months |
| semiannual | six calendar months |
| annual | twelve calendar months |

Hypothetical: a quarterly loan with a due date of 31 August moves its next due date to 30 November, November having no 31st day.

## Points of judgement

- **Both ends of the period count.** A period running from 1 March (the day after a 28 February due date) through 31 March covers 31 days.
- **Final installment.** The last installment is not the level installment amount: it is the billed interest plus all principal then outstanding.
- **Deferred installment.** No bill is booked on the deferred installment's original due date; its interest keeps running until the next due date.
- **Nonaccrual.** Interest is still billed for the record while the loan is in nonaccrual status, but those installments draw no late charge.
